newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish opposition deputy takes government post.
newsitem.headline: Polish opposition deputy takes government post.

text.p: A deputy of Poland's largest opposition party accepted a post in the government led by ex-communists on Thursday -- the latest in a string of defections from the centrist Union for Freedom (UW).

The UW's Katarzyna Piekarska, Poland's youngest parliamentarian aged 29, told reporters she would become deputy minister in the newly-reformed ministry of the interior and administration, headed by Leszek Miller of the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).
"This was a hard decision for me, but it will allow me to get on with work directly involving matters that I was concerned with as a deputy," said Piekarska.

The Union for Freedom groups many of the dissident intellectuals who advised the Solidarity union in its fight for democracy before the 1989 fall of communism, and steered Poland's radical economic reforms afterwards.
But it is now isolated from the bulk of the opposition, notably those parties gathered around Solidarity, which consider it too secular-minded, economically liberal and elitist in style.
Last week six of its deputies quit and joined a Solidarity-linked rightist party, saying the UW was doomed to electoral failure and its left wing might do a deal with its historical foes the SLD.
SLD chiefs dream of such a solution, but Union for Freedom leaders have ruled out any such deal in the near term.
